Article Title: ‘Key growth engine for the world’: IMF hails India’s 7.8% growth, backs GDP estimate changes
Article Text:
IMF hails India’s 7.8% growth, calls economy a key global growth engine

IMF backs changes to GDP estimates

GDP figures face questions

India’s economy has stayed on the growth track despite the energy price shock, with real GDP rising 7.8% in the April-June quarter. The IMF hailed the stronger-than-expected performance, saying that the growth was boosted by better-than-expected activity in services and exports.At a press briefing, IMF spokesperson Julie Kozack said, “India's real GDP in the second quarter grew by 7.8 per cent. That was above our staff's expectations and also the consensus among other observers. This upward surprise was driven by stronger-than-expected activity in the services sector and in exports.”“The outturn also underscores the resilience of the Indian economy despite the energy price shock. It also means that India does remain a key growth engine for the world,” she added.The 7.8% growth in real GDP for Q1 FY27, covering April-June, was higher than the Reserve Bank of India’s earlier estimate of 7%. Data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) showed real GDP at Rs 81.36 lakh crore in the quarter, compared with Rs 75.46 lakh crore in the same period of FY26.Alongside its positive assessment of India’s growth, the IMF also welcomed changes made to the country’s GDP estimation system.Kozack said the latest GDP release included a new index of industrial production and a new producer price index series. According to her, both should help improve India’s GDP estimates.“I can say that the latest GDP release, the one that we just talked about for Q2, it incorporated both a new index of industrial production. It also included a new producer price index series, and those two new series should help improve India's GDP estimates,” Kozack said.She said the IMF welcomed India’s efforts to modernise its macroeconomic statistics and encouraged the authorities to keep strengthening the statistical framework and data quality.“And we welcome these important steps that India is taking to modernise its macroeconomic statistics. And of course, we encourage the authorities to continue to further strengthen the statistical framework and data quality along the lines that they're progressing,” she said.The IMF’s comments come amid a debate over India’s latest GDP numbers and the revisions behind them. Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg had questioned the reported 7.8% growth in the April-June quarter, pointing to a revision in the previous year’s current GDP from Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore.Garg had said that without the revision, growth at current prices would have been around 2.6%, adding to questions over India’s GDP calculations.The IMF also said the latest numbers showed the resilience of India’s economy. It welcomed the changes to the GDP estimation system, noting that the new industrial production index and producer price index series would help improve GDP estimates.
Article Summary: IMF hails India’s 7.8% growth, calls economy a key global growth engine. IMF also welcomed changes made to the country's GDP estimation system. Former finance secretary Subhash Chandra Garg had questioned the reported 7.7% growth.

Article Title: Nitin Gadkari says he felt ‘ashamed’ at Mumbai-Goa highway work delays; ‘I want to set record of blacklisting maximum number of contractors and suspending officials for poor quality work’
Article Text:
He said the government would continue taking stringent action against contractors and officials responsible for delays and substandard execution of infrastructure projects.

‘Want to set record for blacklisting contractors, suspending officials’

Mumbai-Goa highway widening delayed

Union Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari has said that he wants to set a record blacklisting contractors who do poor quality work and also suspend officials.Gadkari said he had earlier expressed shame over the prolonged delay in widening the Mumbai-Goa Highway. He now plans to travel along the highway in October and personally review the work that has been completed.He was speaking after inaugurating a six-lane elevated road corridor at Porvorim near Panaji. Goa Chief Minister Pramod Sawant, Union Minister Shripad Naik, State Public Works Department Minister Digambar Kamat, Tourism Minister Rohan Khaunte and other officials were present at the event.Gadkari said on Wednesday that he wanted to "set a record" by blacklisting the largest possible number of contractors and suspending officials found responsible for delays or poor-quality execution in infrastructure projects."I had announced (earlier) that I would not come for the inauguration of the (widened) Mumbai-Goa highway because I felt ashamed that it had been delayed so much," he said.According to Gadkari, officials held a meeting on the issue on Tuesday."I would land at the Mumbai airport in October, and travel by road to Goa to personally inspect the highway and assess whether the journey has been made convenient for travellers," he said.The minister said the government would continue taking stringent action against contractors and officials responsible for delays and substandard execution of infrastructure projects."Now I want to set a record of blacklisting the maximum number of contractors and taking action against them, as well as suspending officials, within a year. I am not going to stop doing this now," he said.Gadkari also called on the Goa government to develop roadside amenities along the Mumbai-Goa highway that reflect the state's distinctive architecture, cuisine and handicraft traditions.He said these facilities should offer visitors an opportunity to experience Goan food and purchase the state's handloom and handicraft products, giving tourists a distinctive experience as they travel through Goa.Gadkari also proposed adding facilities for biofuels, electric vehicles and other alternative fuels alongside the petrol and diesel pumps operating on the route."If you make a request to me, I am ready to provide them to you," Gadkari said.The widening work on the Mumbai-Goa highway, which runs through Maharashtra's coastal Konkan region, has been delayed repeatedly.He also said landscaping along the highway should be planned scientifically rather than relying on contractors to carry out arbitrary tree plantation."Proper study should be conducted to determine which flowering trees and species should be planted, and which species absorb more carbon dioxide and release oxygen," the minister said.Gadkari appealed to Chief Minister Sawant and local MLAs to support efforts to turn the entire highway into a "green highway". He also suggested that it could be developed along the lines of an "oxygen park".The minister pointed out that he had previously developed an oxygen park in Nagpur.He said quality infrastructure covering water, electricity, transportation and communication is important for attracting investment, generating employment and helping reduce poverty.Gadkari further called for Goa to work towards eliminating water, air and noise pollution. He urged the authorities to ensure that waste does not find its way into the sea.He also sought a comprehensive review of traffic conditions in the state and reforms to address congestion. Among the measures he suggested were consolidating markets, relocating warehouses outside cities, upgrading bus depots and synchronising traffic movement.Referring to the newly inaugurated elevated corridor at Porvorim, Gadkari said a road that originally had a two-lane capacity now effectively provides capacity for ten lanes, with four lanes at ground level and six lanes on the elevated section.The minister also pushed for wider adoption of alternative fuels and technologies such as electric, hydrogen and flex-fuel systems, saying these would contribute to lowering pollution.
Article Summary: Gadkari said he had earlier expressed shame over the prolonged delay in widening the Mumbai-Goa Highway. He now plans to travel along the highway in October and personally review the work that has been completed. He was speaking after inaugurating a six-lane elevated road corridor at Porvorim near Panaji.

Article Title: Rupee tumbles 27 paise against US dollar as crude prices hold firm above $108 per barrel
Article Text:
Rupee falls 27 paise against US dollar

Rupee began Friday on a weak note, falling 27 paise to extend its decline against the US dollar. In early trading, the currency touched 95.79 as high crude oil prices and foreign portfolio outflows continued to weigh it down.Rupee began the session at 95.70 against the dollar at the interbank foreign exchange market before weakening to 95.79. This marked a 27-paise fall from its previous close. Earlier on Thursday, the currency had already lost 44 paise, ending the session at 95.52.According to forex traders, the currency is facing pressure even as India has several factors supporting it. Record foreign exchange reserves, active intervention by the Reserve Bank and robust domestic growth are providing support, but rising global yields and crude prices above $108 are adding to pressure on the country's import bill."For the rupee, the pressure continues. It remains in an uptrend beyond 95 on the back of costly oil and foreign portfolio outflows, and we could see 96, with 95 now acting as support," said Anindya Banerjee, head of commodity and currency research, Kotak Securities.Banerjee said rupee's supporting factors include record foreign exchange reserves, the Reserve Bank's active presence in the market and domestic growth of 7.8 per cent.However, he said the import bill is likely to remain the dominant force in the near term with crude above $100 and global yields rising.Investors are now expected to watch US and Indian inflation data for further direction.The dollar index was at 99.16, up 0.12 per cent. The index measures the strength of the US currency against a basket of six currencies.In the oil market, Brent crude futures were trading 0.76 per cent lower at $108.45 per barrel. The benchmark remained at elevated levels amid escalating US-Iran tensions and concerns over disruption to oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz.Pressure was also visible in the domestic stock market. Sensex fell 628.24 points to 74,257.69 in early trade, while Nifty declined 221.20 points to 23,255.10.Foreign Institutional Investors also remained sellers in the equity market. They offloaded shares worth Rs 438.24 crore on a net basis on Thursday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee began Friday on a weak note, falling 27 paise to extend its decline against the US dollar. In early trading, the currency touched 95.79 as high crude oil prices and foreign portfolio outflows continued to weigh down. Record foreign exchange reserves, active intervention by the Reserve Bank and robust domestic growth are providing support.

Article Title: India’s exports grew over 15% in first five months of FY2026-27, says commerce minister Piyush Goyal
Article Text:
Merchandise exports rose 17.04% to $173.78 billion during April-July, while imports climbed 19.27% to $292.38 billion.

Three hurdles for businesses

Push for common BRICS trade infrastructure

India’s merchandise exports have grown by more than 15 per cent in the first five months of the current fiscal despite a challenging global trade environment, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday.The union minister said the growth highlighted the potential for India and other BRICS economies to deepen trade in goods and services, particularly as businesses navigate geopolitical tensions, trade disruptions and uncertainty.“Despite all the turmoil that the world is going through today...I am happy to share that our merchandise exports from India have grown between April and August, in the first five months of this fiscal, by upward of 15 per cent,” Goyal said at the Brics Women’s Business Alliance (WBA) Women-Led Development Summit 2026, as quoted by PTI.Official trade data for August is due on September 15. In the April-July period, merchandise exports rose 17.04% to $173.78 billion, while imports increased 19.27 per cent to $292.38 billion.Goyal said expanding international trade would require Brics countries to address three key challenges faced by businesses — access to finance, access to buyers and markets, and predictable rules for doing business.He called for greater support for women entrepreneurs and small businesses, including easier access to credit and more opportunities to participate in international trade events.“If we can commit our governments to encourage women-owned enterprises to take greater part in international expositions, conferences, seminars, exhibitions, business forums, it will actually help us engage on many more platforms than an annual Women Business Alliance meeting,” he said.Goyal also proposed more sector-specific women-led business delegations between BRICS countries, giving the example of a women-led textile delegation travelling from one member country to another.The minister pointed to the Jaipur Consensus, agreed upon at the BRICS Commerce and Industry Ministers’ meeting last month, which includes exploring a common BRICS platform for international trade.Such a platform, he said, could help businesses find buyers and enter new markets, while financial intermediaries could provide support to women entrepreneurs and small businesses.Goyal also pushed for greater digital integration in trade, suggesting that BRICS members work towards a common system for electronic trade documents, including e-invoices, electronic bills of lading and e-customs declarations.He said countries should also facilitate cross-border delivery of services online while continuing to respect their respective laws.Goyal said services could also provide another major avenue for expanding intra-BRICS trade. With global services trade approaching $10 trillion, he said the relatively low level of services trade within BRICS points to significant untapped potential.Women entrepreneurs and MSMEs, he said, could play a larger role in areas including mobility, services and the digital economy On financing, Goyal asked the BRICS Women’s Business Alliance and BRICS Business Council to ensure that a proposed study on an invoice discounting platform addresses the actual needs of women exporters.He also urged governments, banks and Exim Banks to consider such invoices while taking lending decisions and called for the proposed Women’s Advancement Fund under the Jaipur Consensus to be turned into a concrete initiative.Goyal said closer cooperation among BRICS economies was important at a time of heightened volatility and uncertainty in global trade, while emphasising that the bloc should continue engaging with the wider global economy.
Article Summary: India’s merchandise exports have grown by more than 15 per cent in the first five months of the current fiscal. In the April-July period, merchandise exports rose 17.04% to $173.78 billion, while imports increased 19.27 per cent to $292.38 billion. Official trade data for August is due on September 15.

Article Title: Indian working in Kuwait sent home over a crore in remittances but filed no ITR; taxman treated Rs 3.63 crore as unexplained, ITAT deletes Rs 5.52 lakh and orders fresh check of Rs 2.50 crore
Article Text:
The absence of an original ITR became a key issue.

What the case is about

What happened in the appeal?

Why did ITAT Ahmedabad partly rule in his favour?

Anilkumar Ramabhai Patel v. ITO

Nitin Mavji Vekariya v. ITO

Why was the Rs 5.52 lakh addition deleted?

Why was the Rs 2.50 crore addition not deleted?

An Indian working in Kuwait and originally from Ahmedabad received an income tax notice after he failed to file an Income Tax Return (ITR), despite remitting more than a crore to his bank accounts in India.The man had moved to Kuwait to work in the oilfields at Mina Al-Ahmadi and had been earning a decent salary. While there, he purchased an insurance policy in India and began sending money to his family back home.His salary was credited to his account with the National Bank of Kuwait, from where he transferred funds to his ICICI and HDFC Bank accounts in India, including NRE and NRO accounts. These transactions came under the Income Tax Department's radar through the Specified Financial Transactions (SFT) reporting system.Banks are required to report specified transactions to the Income Tax Department, and the department's SFT/Insight system showed that, as of December 31, 2018, he had Rs 2.49 crore with HDFC Bank, Rs 1.09 crore with ICICI Bank and an insurance policy worth Rs 3.77 lakh with ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company.The absence of an original ITR became a key issue. Although the department had information about the substantial sums held in his Indian accounts, there was no tax return on record explaining their nature and source.The Income Tax Assessing Officer from the International Taxation wing in Ahmedabad consequently issued a notice asking him to explain the money in his bank accounts and the insurance policy.The man subsequently filed an ITR declaring nil income. The tax officer then sought detailed information, including his NRE and NRO bank statements, details of time deposits, an explanation of the SFT figures and a reconciliation of the amounts reported by the banks.The man provided only limited information, primarily his NRE account statement. He did not submit the complete documentation required to explain the reported balances, nor did he provide a reconciliation showing how the cumulative SFT figures had been calculated.The AO therefore treated the entire Rs 3.63 crore reported through SFT as unexplained money under Section 69A. Since there were no documents before the AO establishing that the funds represented foreign remittances, accumulated savings or another identifiable source, the amount was taxed under Section 115BBE. His assessed income was consequently determined at Rs 3.63 crore.The man challenged the assessment and, during the appellate proceedings, filed an application under Rule 46A seeking admission of additional evidence.The documents included statements of his National Bank of Kuwait account, salary details from his employer, Indian NRE account statements and other records intended to establish the movement of his Kuwait earnings into his Indian accounts.The Commissioner of Appeals (CIT A) sought a remand report from the AO. During the remand proceedings, the AO examined the additional evidence and issued notices under Section 133(6) to ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company to verify the SFT-reported figures.The remand proceedings established that the man was earning a good salary in Kuwait. His salary was credited to his National Bank of Kuwait account and subsequently remitted to India through proper banking channels into his NRE accounts with ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank. This explained the source of certain deposits, particularly the fixed deposits with ICICI Bank.However, the SFT figures could not be fully matched with the actual bank statements. The man argued in his rejoinder that if the AO himself could not reconcile the figures, it was unreasonable to expect him to do so.The CIT (A) deleted the additions relating to the ICICI Bank account and the insurance policy but retained the Rs 2.49 crore HDFC Bank addition and Rs 5.52 lakh as unexplained money.The matter then reached the ITAT Ahmedabad. S. N. Divatia and Samir Vora represented the man before the ITAT Ahmedabad D Bench, comprising Smt Annapurna Gupta, Accountant Member, and Mr Siddhartha Nautiyal, Judicial Member. The tribunal passed its order on April 24, 2026, granting partial relief.The tribunal relied on two Gujarat High Court rulings,[2025] 178 taxmann.com 634 (Guj.) and[461 ITR 18 (Guj.)]. The principle from these decisions is that where funds in an NRE account are shown to have originated from foreign earnings, Section 69A cannot be applied to treat those funds as unexplained money.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana told ET that the man's NRI status, his employment in Kuwait and his NRE accounts were undisputed. There was also evidence showing that his overseas salary was first credited to his National Bank of Kuwait account and then remitted to India through banking channels.The tribunal found that the Rs 5.52 lakh addition relating to ICICI Bank arose from the inability to reconcile the cumulative SFT figure with the actual bank records.The Income Tax Department had not produced independent evidence establishing that this amount represented undisclosed income or came from an unexplained source. Since a substantial portion of the same account had already been accepted as having originated from foreign salary remittances, the tribunal found no sufficient basis to treat the residual Rs 5.52 lakh as unexplained.The addition was therefore deleted.The tribunal took a different view of the approximately Rs 2.50 crore reported in relation to HDFC Bank. It noted that the addition was based on a cumulative SFT figure, without transaction-wise details or supporting material establishing what the amount represented.Surana says: “Despite a notice issued under Section 133(6), HDFC Bank did not provide the required information, and even the Assessing Officer could not ascertain or reconcile the basis of the reported figure.”The basis of the addition therefore remained unverified. However, the tribunal also noted that the man had not furnished a complete one-to-one reconciliation himself.It consequently sent the HDFC Bank issue back to the Assessing Officer for fresh verification rather than deleting the addition outright. The tribunal directed that no addition should be made if the funds are found to represent foreign income remitted to India or the subsequent redeployment of those funds.The appeal was thus partly allowed for statistical purposes. The Rs 5.52 lakh addition was deleted, while the approximately Rs 2.50 crore HDFC Bank addition was remanded for fresh examination.
Article Summary: An Indian working in Kuwait and originally from Ahmedabad received an income tax notice after he failed to file an Income Tax Return (ITR) The man had moved to Kuwait to work in the oilfields at Mina Al-Ahmadi and had been earning a decent salary. While there, he purchased an insurance policy in India and began sending money to his family back home. These transactions came under the Income Tax Department's radar through the Specified Financial Transactions system.

Article Title: Efficiency booster: BLR becomes first south Asian airport to implement system for more efficient flight arrivals
Article Text:
Bengaluru's Kempegowda airport becomes first in South Asia to implement point merge system, reducing congestion, fuel burn and emissions for arriving aircraft.

NEW DELHI: Flying into Bengaluru will soon mean reduced congestion and shorter hovering for aircraft as the garden city’s Kempegowda Int’l Airport (BLR) has become the first airport in South Asia to implement “point merge system”. This is an area navigation procedure that allows air traffic controllers to sequence inbound aircraft onto the final approach. Akasa’s flight Mumbai-BLR flight QP 1129 became the first flight to use this newly introduced system on Wednesday.Akasa said on X: “An initiative by Airports Authority of India (AAI) and Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), point merge helps arriving aircraft move through the skies in a smoother, smarter and more organised way. This can make arrivals more predictable, reduce unnecessary flying time and communication, and help lower fuel consumption and emissions. Already in use at airports around the world, its introduction in BLR is an exciting step forward for Indian aviation. ”BIAL did not comment on this. It is learnt the trials will be on for three months before the rollout.Currently operational at 59 airports in 23 countries, point merge system enables aircraft to fly along published sequencing legs and when it is considered that there is adequate spacing, the controller will instruct the pilot to route direct to the “merge point”.It allows for more efficient and optimum utilisation of available airspace.Giving the benefits for airlines under the new system, a senior pilot said: “This leads to enhanced operational efficiency and consistency by creating a system which reduces the gaps of individual controller vectoring techniques. There’s enhanced predictability; reduced congestion and fuel consumptions due to efficient inter arrival spacing”Another pilot said: “Point merge reduces radio telephony (RT) congestion and leads to less RT workload for the pilots and air traffic controllers. It becomes easier to accommodate priority/emergency aircraft. There is less effect of winds on sequencing as all the arriving aircraft approaches from almost same directions.”A third pilot said all these steps lead to enhanced safety. “Aircraft can maintain a more efficient descent profile and use continuous descent operations (CDO). Less fuel burn directly reduces the airline’s direct operating cost. Reduced airborne time also reduces engine operating time and associated maintenance exposure. These benefits become significant when multiplied across hundreds of daily arrivals. Reduced holding and delay. Instead of frequent heading and speed instructions from ATC, the aircraft follows a predefined sequencing leg and receives a relatively simple ‘direct to merge point’ instruction,” he said.The biggest airline benefit is not simply “shorter routes.” They are: predictable sequencing plus reduced vectoring; reduced level-offs plus; CDO; reduced airborne delay; lower fuel burn and more predictable operations.
Article Summary: Bengaluru's Kempegowda airport becomes first in South Asia to implement point merge system. System allows air traffic controllers to sequence inbound aircraft onto final approach. Already in use at airports around the world, its introduction in BLR is an exciting step forward for Indian aviation.

Article Title: Apple raises prices of older iPhones ahead of festive sales
Article Text:
Apple iPhone 17 (For representative purpose only)

NEW DELHI: Buying an iPhone has become costlier in India and even older iPhones will now cost more. Apple has raised prices across its India line-up ahead of festive sales, making the jump to a new handset more expensive for buyers.The increases cover iPhone 16, iPhone 17e, iPhone Air and newly launched iPhone 18 Pro series. They also affect higher storage variants, with some of the sharpest revisions appearing beyond the starting configurations. Traditionally, Apple slashes prices of previous generation iPhones when it launches a new model. In the last few years, the reduction was to the tune of Rs 10,000.India faces substantially steeper increases for the new Pro models than the US and UK. Launch prices for the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max are about 22% and 20% above their predecessors, respectively, compared with increases of 9% and 8% in those markets.The difference puts the focus on what Indian consumers must pay for the same generational upgrade. Meanwhile, increases on existing devices mean choosing an older model does not shelter buyers from the latest pricing revisions.Storage upgrades have become more expensive too. The prices of 512GB iPhone 17 has risen by Rs 22,000, while 1TB iPhone Air costs Rs 65,000 more than before, an increase of 40.7%.These are increases on the devices themselves, rather than comparisons between successive Pro generations.The revised prices arrive as buyers prepare for festive shopping. For consumers comparing models, the distinction between official prices and the final purchase cost will matter. Retailer discounts, exchange benefits and payment offers will determine the eventual bill.
Article Summary: Apple has raised prices across its India line-up ahead of festive sales. The increases cover iPhone 16, iPhone 17e, iPhone Air and newly launched iPhone 18 Pro series. Traditionally, Apple slashes prices of previous generation iPhones when it launches a new model.

Article Title: Small towns power Quick-commerce biz for Flipkart
Article Text: MUMBAI: Small towns are fueling the growth of Flipkart’s quick commerce business Minutes. Cities such as Siliguri, Ambala, Barabanki, Bhagalpur and Durgapur are seeing huge consumer adoption with the overall customer base growing nearly 25 times year-on-year across such regions, the Walmart-owned company said.The broader Minutes business has expanded four times y-o-y since its launch two years back. Minutes has now widened its footprint to nearly 1,200 dark stores covering more than 150 cities. In a statement, Flipkart said that around 60% of customers return to shop on Minutes. The instant delivery business rivals Amazon’s Now, Eternal’s Blinkit, Swiggy’s Instamart and Zepto.In an interaction, Kunal Gupta, Senior Vice President and Head of Flipkart Minutes said that demand on the platform has grown beyond everyday essentials with consumers also shopping for gourmet and premium products. Gourmet and specialty grocery, launched within the past year, has grown eight times, led by demand for cold-pressed oils, imported cheeses, international avocado varieties and Korean ready-to-eat meals. In fact, consumers are adding products such as Korean noodles, sauces and ready-to-eat meals, alongside premium skincare and personal care categories even in smaller cities.Flipkart is understood to be piloting a standalone app for Minutes with a wider rollout is expected ahead of its annual festive sales in October.“We believe a standalone app would help create a sharper identity for Minutes as a QC platform rather than keeping it embedded within Flipkart’s broader e-commerce proposition. The timing also appears favourable, with the wider rollout planned ahead of BBD (Big Billion Days), a period of significantly higher consumer traffic and engagement for Flipkart – which would provide an opportunity to drive initial discovery and awareness of the Minutes app,” analysts at JM Financial said in a note.Among consumer cohorts, Gen Z has emerged as the fastest-growing customer cohort on Minutes, with the customer base growing nearly five times y-o-y in the past twelve months. Gen Z drives over 45% of orders across categories such as beauty, electronics, gaming, wearables, fragrance, health and nutrition, and grooming, the firm said."In two years, Flipkart Minutes has evolved from a convenience offering into a broader shopping channel, with customers using it for much more than their daily essentials. What is particularly interesting is how quickly this behaviour is spreading beyond the largest cities, while Gen Z is also bringing new categories and new shopping occasions to the platform. With our growing network, we have an opportunity to make this experience available to more consumers across the country, while creating new opportunities for brands, farmers and local businesses to reach customers,” Gupta said.
Article Summary: Small towns are fueling the growth of Flipkart’s quick commerce business Minutes. Cities such as Siliguri, Ambala, Barabanki, Bhagalpur and Durgapur are seeing huge consumer adoption. The overall customer base growing nearly 25 times year-on-year across such regions.

Article Title: Surplus liquidity crosses 11 lakh crore in money market
Article Text: MUMBAI: Surplus liquidity in India's money market has crossed Rs 11 lakh crore, leaving Reserve Bank of India to mop up an unusually large pool of cash unleashed by banks' $136 billion mobilisation of foreign-currency deposits. The central bank has responded with a battery of operations, seeking to prevent an excess of rupees from pushing short-term rates too far below its policy rate.RBI has absorbed more than Rs 4.6 lakh crore through 30-day variable-rate reverse repos (VRRR), and another Rs 6.6 lakh crore through overnight repos and standing deposit facility (SDF) operations. It has also used dollar-rupee buy-sell swaps with banks to drain liquidity. By taking dollars out of the market and supplying them forward, these swaps raise the dollar's forward premium while easing immediate demand for dollars in the spot market, reducing pressure on the rupee.The liquidity deluge is an unintended consequence of a special concessional swap window designed to strengthen India's external balances. Data through Aug 31 showed that the facility attracted $136.4 billion of foreign-currency inflows, including $127.2 billion through FCNR(B) deposits.Banks swapped the dollars with RBI for rupees, releasing a large quantity of domestic liquidity into the banking system.The question is what banks will do with the cash. Axis Bank MD & CEO Amitabh Chaudhry warned that the inflows could result in "abnormal lending", reminding markets of past excesses of banks.SBI chairman CS Setty is less worried as he does not expect the liquidity surplus to distort credit growth, which has been expanding at 18.3% year-on-year, and expects the excess liquidity to be absorbed within a quarter.The inflows accelerated in Aug as banks offered higher rates to non-resident depositors, while RBI absorbed the associated hedging costs. Sneha Pandey, fund manager at Quantum AMC, said the monthly increase was particularly sharp. "While core liquidity crossed Rs 10 lakh crore, the daily average surplus stood at Rs 3.67 lakh crore in Aug, more than three times July's Rs 1.07 lakh crore."Banks initially preferred to keep the money close at hand rather than commit it to longer-term assets. "RBI has been running back-to-back Variable Rate Reverse Repo (VRRR) auctions on successive days... banks prefer to park at 1 to 3 days and keep their powder dry for credit demand," Pandey said.The effect is showing up in money-market rates. As system liquidity crossed Rs 10 lakh crore, the weighted average call rate fell below 5% to 4.96%, slipping below RBI's policy repo rate. On the other hand, yields in the longer-duration papers have hardened.The surge in FCNR(B) inflows has strengthened India's external position, but it has also created a significant liquidity overhang that RBI will need to manage carefully, said Ram Kamal Samanta, CIO, Star Union Dai-ichi Life Insurance.On the rupee front, according to Radhika Rao, senior economist and ED, DBS Bank, the foreign-currency inflows had compounded an already substantial rupee surplus. "Given the swap arrangement, these inflows will add to an already abundant rupee liquidity backdrop, which was at a four-year high this month, depressing overnight rates."
Article Summary: RBI has absorbed more than Rs 4.6 lakh crore through 30-day variable-rate reverse repos. It has also used dollar-rupee buy-sell swaps with banks to drain liquidity. Axis Bank MD & CEO Amitabh Chaudhry warned that the inflows could result in "abnormal lending"

Article Title: Gross SIP flows, fund industry assets at record high
Article Text: MUMBAI: Discounting volatility in the stock market, investors poured in money through the mutual fund route that led to a record Rs 32,297 crore in gross monthly inflows through the systematic investment plan (SIP) route in Aug. This, combined with strong buying across most equity mutual fund categories, lifted the total assets managed by the fund industry to just a tad above the Rs 87 lakh crore mark, also a new all-time high level, data from industry trade body AMFI showed.According to Navneet Munot, MD & CEO of HDFC AMC, in Aug, the fund industry extended a trend that has been observed for some time now as SIP inflows climbed to a record high even as the market remained volatile on global cues.AMFI data showed that as of Aug 31, SIP assets stood at Rs 18.6 lakh crore, up 2.8% on the month, while the number of contributing SIP accounts was at a little over 10 crore.During the month, net inflows into equity schemes were Rs 29,329 crore. This was the 66th consecutive month of net inflows through this fund category. Among equity fund categories, while small-cap funds took in a net Rs 7,973 crore, mid-cap schemes recorded net inflows worth Rs 6,989 crore, and flexicap funds Rs 5,059 crore.AMFI data also showed that in Aug, retail folios (equity + hybrid + solutions-oriented schemes) were at 21.6 crore, up from 21.4 crore the previous month.According to Saugata Chatterjee, president & deputy CEO, Nippon India Mutual Fund, the continued growth in industry folios was the most encouraging takeaway from Aug data that reflected the widening reach of mutual funds. "Record-high SIP contributions, along with a moderating stoppage ratio, further demonstrate the growing discipline of Indian investors. The continued preference for small-cap and mid-cap funds indicates investors' desire to participate in the broader opportunity across corporate India. Given the nature of these segments, disciplined allocation, patience and a longer investment horizon remain important."
Article Summary: Investors poured in money through the mutual fund route that led to a record Rs 32,297 crore in gross monthly inflows through the systematic investment plan (SIP) route in Aug. This, combined with strong buying across most equity mutual fund categories, lifted the total assets managed by the fund industry to a new all-time high level.

Article Title: Emerging sectors to drive next industrial revolution: Report
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Emerging sectors, such as space, data centers, solar energy, semiconductors and electronics are set to drive the next phase of industrial revolution in India as the large domestic opportunity is driving private participation.Supportive govt policies, such as tax holidays for establishing data centres, large incentive schemes for boosting semiconductor production, electronics and solar cells, along with promoting greater private participation in the space sector, are some of the policies that will drive growth in these industries, a report by global investment banker Jefferies has said.The report said India's next industrial revolution is being built on an already significant manufacturing base in select industries, such as steel, cement, automobiles and oil refineries. "The combination of scale, domestic demand, manufacturing capabilities and policy support provides a strong foundation for the country's next growth engines in (these industries)," the report said.In the space sector, the report noted that India is among a handful of spacefaring nations with "global competitive capabilities" and govt is targeting nearly five times expansion in the space economy to $40-50 billion over 2023-30.From just one space startup in 2014 to over 400 in 2026, investor interest is rising with cumulative private investment reaching $600 million by 2025-26. "Indian space start-ups are now progressing from early stage innovation to commercial execution. "In semiconductors, the report said India's aspirations are moving from policy intent to execution with nearly $20 billion of investments, including a chip fab under construction. A new $13 billion incentive plan should further expand the ecosystem and boost value addition, including chip design.Regarding data centres, the report said the space is rapidly emerging as a strategic digital infrastructure segment, with colocation capacity expanding five times over the past five years to 2 GW (gigawatt). "Capacity is expected to grow another five times to nearly 10GW over the next five years, supported by favourable cost economics, policy support and rising hyperscale demand."
Article Summary: The report said India's next industrial revolution is being built on an already significant manufacturing base in select industries. The report noted that India is among a handful of spacefaring nations with "global competitive capabilities" and govt is targeting nearly five times expansion in the space economy to $40-50 billion over 2023-30.

Article Title: Apple's foldable debut to lift mkt, test Samsung
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Apple could bring more buyers to foldables without winning most of them. Foldable phones have flexible screens that let them open into larger displays or fold into more compact devices. The Cupertino-based company's entry with the iPhone Duo is expected to draw attention to a smartphone category that remains small in India, while Samsung's wider price range could help it capture much of the increase in sales.At Rs 2,99,900, the Duo gives iPhone users a foldable within Apple's ecosystem. Its immediate contribution, however, could be greater in consumer awareness, developer interest and market value than in shipment volumes."Samsung has been building this category for years, and its pricing spread across multiple foldable form factors only strengthens that position for now," said Upasana Joshi of IDC India.India's foldable shipments stood at just under 6.3 lakh units in 2025, against total smartphone shipments of 15.2 crore, according to IDC. Samsung accounted for the vast majority. IDC expects foldable shipments to reach 8-8.5 lakh units in 2026, even as overall smartphone shipments decline to around 12.5 crore.Joshi said Apple's pricing would keep the Duo largely within the super-premium segment initially, limiting the volumes it could generate to challenge Samsung's leadership.Counterpoint Research's Tarun Pathak expects India's foldable market to cross 10 lakh units next year, with Samsung driving much of that expansion because of its price advantage. Apple could encourage developers to build better experiences and help consumers understand the category."The bigger message is that foldables are moving beyond being just a technology showcase and becoming a more established premium smartphone category," Pathak said. India has an installed base of around 30 lakh foldables against more than 74 crore smartphone users, according to Pathak. He does not expect the category to become mass market for another three-to-four years.For Apple, the commercial opportunity extends beyond unit sales. Prabhu Ram of CyberMedia Research described the Duo as "a halo offering to elevate overall portfolio ASPs", positioning it above the flagship lineup for affluent buyers. Apple's entry could reinforce shift towards wider, book-style foldables, which Pathak said offer a more natural tablet-like experience for documents, video and multitasking.
Article Summary: Apple's entry with the iPhone Duo is expected to draw attention to a smartphone category that remains small in India. At Rs 2,99,900, the Duo gives iPhone users a foldable within Apple's ecosystem. Samsung's wider price range could help it capture much of the increase in sales.

Article Title: 'Building tomorrow's market today with tokenised bonds'
Article Text: MUMBAI: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said early experiments with financial asset tokenisation were helping the regulator test the infrastructure for future markets as he launched a pilot enabling instant settlement of tokenised corporate bonds through the eRupee.Malhotra on Thursday launched the Demat 2.0 pilot with Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey at the Global Fintech Fest. The initiative enables corporate bonds to be tokenised and settled through the central bank digital currency, while automating coupon payments and redemption.RBI is also looking to expand the Unified Lending Interface (ULI) as common digital rails for consent-based credit delivery. It plans to roll out the proposed Digital Payments Intelligence Platform alongside MuleHunter.ai to strengthen real-time fraud mitigation. The central bank is continuing programmable CBDC pilots for targeted govt benefit transfers, including PMGKAY, while expanding the wholesale CBDC market architecture.He said AI, quantum computing and tokenisation should be applied to practical problems such as improving consumer services, addressing credit gaps, increasing operational efficiency and reducing fraud. At the same time, firms need to address risks from algorithmic opacity, bias, financial exclusion, herding behaviour, cybersecurity vulnerabilities, data privacy and the erosion of human judgement in AI-based decision-making.The governor also stressed that customer data should be treated as a fiduciary responsibility, with its use bound by purpose and consent rather than treated as an asset to be monetised.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said early experiments with financial asset tokenisation were helping the regulator test the infrastructure for future markets. He launched a pilot enabling instant settlement of tokenised corporate bonds through the eRupee. The initiative enables corporate bonds to be tokenised and settled through the central bank digital currency.

Article Title: IIT Roorkee researchers develop self-powered smart bandage that uses body movement to support wound healing
Article Text:
IIT Roorkee develops battery-free smart bandage powered by natural body movement

Smart scaffold combines electrical stimulation and flexibility

IIT Roorkee researchers create self-powered wound dressing with 90–95% closure in animal studies

Laboratory and animal studies show healing response

IIT Roorkee develops battery-free electronic bandage using natural movement to generate healing-supporting signals

Device tested for repeated mechanical deformation

Study published in Nano Energy

Researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee (IIT Roorkee), in collaboration with the Institute of Nano Science and Technology (INST), Mohali, have developed a self-powered electronic bandage that uses natural body movement to generate electrical signals that can support wound healing. The technology does not require batteries, wires or an external power source.Called 3D-MIDAS, or 3D Monolithic Integrated Dipolar-Ionic Fibrous Architectural Scaffold, the technology converts mechanical energy generated when its flexible material stretches during body movement into electrical stimulation at the wound site.The 3D-MIDAS scaffold combines electrically active nanofibres with an ionically conductive network in a three-dimensional fibrous structure. When stretched, the integrated components generate electrical signals. The scaffold can stretch to approximately 800% of its original length, enabling it to accommodate natural body movement.Its porous structure also provides breathability and supports wound-fluid management. The technology is designed to address the disruption of natural electrical signals involved in guiding cells during tissue repair after skin injury.Prof. K. K. Pant, Director, IIT Roorkee, said the research brings together advanced materials and interdisciplinary expertise to address a healthcare requirement through a self-powered approach.The researchers evaluated 3D-MIDAS through laboratory and animal studies. Laboratory experiments showed approximately three-fold higher cell proliferation and 2.5-fold greater cell migration compared with control conditions.In animal studies, wounds treated with the dressing recorded approximately 90–95% wound closure within 13–15 days, along with increased formation of new blood vessels. Histological analysis showed improved tissue architecture and enhanced collagen deposition in treated wounds.The dressing also generated electrical output when placed on wounds of freely moving rats, without externally applied mechanical stimulation.The device maintained stable electrical performance over 500 stretching cycles. Longer-term testing demonstrated stable performance over three months. Researchers also assessed cell compatibility, blood compatibility, inflammatory responses and tissue regeneration.Prof. Kaushik Parida, Principal Investigator, IIT Roorkee, said the technology was developed to overcome the requirement for an external power source in many electrical wound-healing systems.The self-powered design could have future applications in remote healthcare, emergency and disaster-response settings. However, the present study did not evaluate military use, and no defence application has been established. Human clinical studies will be required before routine medical use.The research has been published in the peer-reviewed journal Nano Energy under the title “3D monolithic integrated dipolar-ionic fibrous scaffold for self-powered wound healing and exudate management”. The study appears in Volume 157 (2026), Article 112266.The research was supported by the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF), Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), Department of Science and Technology (DST) and Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship (PMRF).The research team included Prof. Kaushik Parida, Vishu Verma, Romy Garg, Sayanti Mallick and Aneesh Ali from IIT Roorkee, and Kanika, Jattin Kumar and Rehan Khan from INST, Mohali.
Article Summary: IIT Roorkee develops battery-free smart bandage powered by natural body movement. Smart scaffold combines electrical stimulation and flexibility. Wounds treated with the dressing recorded approximately 90–95% wound closure within 13–15 days, along with increased formation of new blood vessels.

Article Title: Oil touches $107 per barrel as Hormuz remains choked for over six months
Article Text:
Oil crosses $100 again as Middle East attacks fuel supply fears

Hormuz conflict intensifies

China could determine how far prices go

OPEC cuts demand forecast

Oil prices extended their gains on Friday, with both major benchmarks on track to finish the week above $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May, as growing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East heightened concerns over prolonged supply disruptions.Around 7:30 am IST, Brent crude was trading at $107.70 a barrel, up 0.03%, while WTI crude stood at $102.50 a barrel, unchanged. Both benchmarks had surged more than 6% on Thursday, taking their weekly gains to nearly 13%, the steepest increase since the week ended July 17.The latest rise came as risks to oil shipments increased across both the Red Sea and the Gulf. Iran-aligned Houthis seized control of Yemen's port of Mocha on Thursday, posing a further threat to Red Sea traffic, while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains restricted amid intensified tanker attacks in recent days.The attacks from Yemen on Saudi energy facilities have added another layer of risk to the oil market, with concerns now extending beyond Iran and the Strait of Hormuz.US President Donald Trump warned that the US may hit Iran's Pickaxe Mountain, located near its heavily damaged Natanz uranium enrichment facility, and said the war would likely last beyond the November midterm elections.Iran said it had attacked 10 ships near the strait on Wednesday, after the US hit five Iranian oil tankers.Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it would escalate its response to any further attacks.The impact of the attacks has also been reflected in US fuel prices. The US national average price of diesel surpassed $6 a gallon for the first time ever on Thursday, according to price tracker GasBuddy, as the US-Iran war and Ukrainian attacks on Russia's refineries have squeezed supply.Analysts said the durability of the oil rally will depend heavily on China, the world's largest crude importer.China has stepped up purchases in recent weeks after months of subdued demand, boosting physical crude markets, ING analysts said in a note. Continued buying could amplify the impact of supply disruptions and push prices higher, while a pullback in imports could temper market gains.OPEC has lowered its forecast for world oil demand growth in 2026 to 380,000 barrels per day, according to a copy of its monthly report. It was the fifth straight downward revision to its demand growth forecast.OPEC oil output also fell by 640,000 barrels per day in August, a Reuters survey found, as Saudi exports faced new disruptions due to the war in Iran and a US blockade cut Iran's shipments.Meanwhile, US crude oil inventories fell by 391,000 barrels to 424.1 million barrels last week as refining activity continued to show strength, the Energy Information Administration said.
Article Summary: Brent crude was trading at $107.70 a barrel on Friday morning, up 0.03%. WTI crude stood at $102.50 a barrel, unchanged. Both benchmarks had surged more than 6% on Thursday, taking their weekly gains to nearly 13%.

Article Title: Iran-China oil barter system keeps billions flowing despite US sanctions: Report
Article Text:
China accounted for more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil exports in 2025, at an average of about 1.4 million barrels per day, according to Kpler data.

How the system works

Oil turned into import credit: Instead of Iranian buyers directly paying Chinese companies through international banking channels, proceeds from Iranian oil sales are placed into a system that creates credits for purchases from China.

Instead of Iranian buyers directly paying Chinese companies through international banking channels, proceeds from Iranian oil sales are placed into a system that creates credits for purchases from China. Oil remains the foundation: China accounted for more than 80 per cent of Iran's shipped oil exports in 2025, at an average of about 1.4 million barrels per day, according to Kpler data.

Iran has been using a barter-like system to trade its oil for goods from China, allowing Tehran to bypass conventional international banking channels and keep billions of dollars in trade flowing despite US sanctions, according to Reuters.Under the arrangement, Iranian oil proceeds are converted into credits that can be used to pay Chinese suppliers, according to sources cited by Reuters. The system has been used for medicines, vehicles and communication equipment and, at least once in the past year, for contracts linked to air defence equipment, sources familiar with the matter told Reuters.The mechanism has also allowed China, the biggest buyer of Iranian crude, to continue accessing discounted oil while limiting the exposure of Chinese banks and exporters to international sanctions.The arrangement, described by Reuters, illustrates how Iran and China have maintained trade despite US sanctions and restrictions on Tehran's oil exports. The US has sanctioned some Chinese entities involved in Iranian oil trade, but has so far avoided the most sweeping measures that could have wider effects on the global economy.However, China's foreign ministry, responding to Reuters' questions, said it was “not familiar with the situation you describe.”“China has consistently opposed unilateral sanctions that have no basis in international law and have not been authorized by the United Nations Security Council,” it said.The arrangement could face greater pressure from the US blockade of Iran. Reuters reported last week that no Iranian crude cargoes had successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz to China since the blockade was reinstated on July 14.
